rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Linear momentum, $\vec p = m\vec v$, is the vector "quantity of motion"; its rate of change is force — Newton's second law in the form $\vec F = d\vec p/dt$. Impulse, $\vec J = \vec F\Delta t$, measures the momentum delivered by a push: $\vec F\Delta t = \Delta\vec p$.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - p⃗ = mv⃗ - J⃗ = F⃗Δt = Δp⃗ = mv⃗ − mu⃗ - F⃗ = dp⃗/dt; constant mass → F⃗ = ma⃗

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Momentum vs kinetic energy:** momentum p = mv (vector, conserved in all collisions); KE = ½mv² (scalar, conserved only in elastic ones).  ·  **Impulse vs force:** impulse is force × time — the same push spread over longer time delivers smaller force.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Momentum is the currency of motion — forces are its exchange rate in time."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Gun recoil*** — 5 kg gun, 10 g bullet at 400 m/s → recoil 0.8 m/s (NEB 2024).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Verified PYQs: gun recoil (2024, 3m); force from momentum change (2023, 3m).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Mass in Motion Momentum ($\vec p = m\vec v$) is "quantity of motion" — the conserved currency of collisions, explosions and rocketry. Impulse is momentum's change per push. This topic defines both and sets up conservation (next topic).  ·  ## 2. rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "FΔt = Δp — the longer the push, the gentler the force."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (3m): A 60 g ball hits a bat at 20 m/s and returns along the same line at 30 m/s. If contact lasts 0.02 s, find the average force.** — Take the return direction positive: Δp = m(v−u) = 0.06(30 − (−20)) = 0.06 × 50 = 3 kg·m/s; F = Δp/Δt = 3/0.02 = 150 N. Direction reversal doubles the momentum change.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Most-tested: recoil numerical (2024). Always convert grams to kilograms before substituting.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Longer time, smaller force:** the impulse–momentum theorem is why airbags, crumple zones and "riding the catch" save lives — same Δp, more time, less F.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: p⃗ = mv⃗ (kg·m/s, vector); J⃗ = F⃗Δt = Δp⃗ (N·s).  ·  Newton's second law in momentum form: F⃗ = dp⃗/dt.  ·  Recoil: m_g v_g + m_b v_b = 0 → v_g = −m_b v_b/m_g.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: A rocket in empty space accelerates by throwing mass backward — momentum conservation needs no ground to push against.

rows.text: ## 3. Worked Numericals **Q1 (3m, 2024):** A gun of mass 5 kg fires a bullet of mass 10 g with velocity 400 m/s. Calculate the recoil velocity of the gun. *Given:* $m_g = 5$ kg, $m_b = 0.01$ kg, $v_b = 400$ m/s; initial momentum zero. *Conservation:* $m_g v_g + m_b v_b = 0 → v_g = -m_b v_b/m_g = -(0.01 \times 400)/5 = -0.8$ m/s.…  ·  ## 4.
